metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Brownsville, PA | Fayette Co.
metaDescription: Brownsville, PA mineral owners: get a straightforward cash offer on your oil and gas interest along the Monongahela in Fayette County.
heroLead: Brownsville is one of the older river towns in Fayette County, and its surrounding land carries more layers of mineral history than most.
intro: Brownsville sits along the Monongahela in a part of Fayette County that's had industry and mining running through it for close to two centuries. If your family holds mineral rights connected to this area, the ownership picture may run through an old coal severance, a mid-century conventional oil or gas lease, and, on some tracts, more recent Marcellus or Utica activity, all layered on top of each other across generations of deeds.
We take the time to trace each layer individually rather than assuming the newest lease tells the whole story. That's the only way to get an honest answer about what you actually own.

sections.heading: A county with a longer mineral history than most
paragraphs: Fayette County's coal and coke history predates the Marcellus boom by more than a century, and Brownsville sat near the center of that industry. Coal severances from this era are common, and they typically affected only the coal seam, leaving oil and gas rights with the family unless a separate transaction addressed them too.
More recently, unconventional development has reached parts of Fayette County, targeting the Marcellus and, in places, the deeper Utica and Point Pleasant formations.

sections.heading: What we look for in Brownsville-area title work
paragraphs: We trace your chain of title through the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds, checking each historical transaction for what was actually conveyed versus what was reserved, so the picture we give you reflects the real legal history, not a family assumption passed down over the years.

sections.heading: From confirmed ownership to a real offer
paragraphs: Once your ownership is confirmed, we check current leasing and production activity and build a number around what your specific interest is actually generating or likely to generate.

faqs.question: How far back do coal severances in this area typically go?
faqs.answer: Often to the late 1800s or early 1900s, when coal companies acquired seam rights across much of Fayette County while landowners frequently kept the oil and gas.

faqs.question: Is Marcellus drilling actually happening near Brownsville?
faqs.answer: Development has reached parts of Fayette County, though less densely than counties further west. We'll confirm activity specific to your parcel.

faqs.question: What if my family's deed doesn't clearly say what was reserved?
faqs.answer: That's common with older documents. We interpret the deed language against Pennsylvania law and historical practice to determine what was most likely retained.
